items: Class: A blueprint or template that defines an object’s state (fields) and behavior (methods). Example: A Customer class defines what a customer "is" and "can do".
Object: A real-world entity created from a class. It represents a specific instance of the class. Example: Customer c1 = new Customer(); — c1 is an object.
Definition: Abstraction is the process of exposing only essential details while hiding unnecessary implementation details from the user.
Example: A Banking Application has users like Branch Manager, Accountant, and Cashier. Each sees only relevant parts of the system based on their role.
Definition: Wrapping data (variables) and code (methods) into a single unit and restricting direct access to some components.
Example: A Customer class has a private field accountBalance. It is accessed only through the public method getBalance().
Definition: Enables a class (child/subclass) to inherit properties and behavior from another class (parent/superclass).
Example: Loan is the superclass with common attributes. HomeLoan, CarLoan, and GoldLoan are subclasses that reuse and extend the common features.
Definition: The ability of a single function or method to operate in different ways depending on the object.
